Reporting to the Head of Environment & Sustainability, you will define and deliver the environmental strategy for the STEP programme and provide programme-level assurance that environmental and sustainability risks are effectively understood, managed, and controlled throughout the full lifecycle of the power plant.
As a senior leader within UKFE, you will ensure environmental performance is embedded into engineering, construction, operational, and strategic decision-making. You will lead the development of a proportionate, evidence-based Environmental Case and provide leadership across environmental consenting, permitting, regulatory engagement, and sustainability performance.
This is a high-profile position operating in a unique technological environment where regulatory frameworks continue to evolve. Your expertise will help shape how fusion energy is responsibly delivered for future generations.

Environmental Strategy & Programme Leadership
• Define and deliver the environmental strategy across your allocated area of responsibility within the STEP programme.
• Provide senior environmental leadership across engineering, construction, operations, and programme delivery functions.
• Ensure environmental considerations are integrated into programme design, delivery, and operational decision-making.
• Balance innovation with regulatory compliance, environmental stewardship, and societal expectations.
Building Environmental Capability

• Lead the development and ongoing justification of the programme's Environmental Case.

• Ensure environmental risks are identified, assessed, managed, and visible to support informed decision-making.

• Ensure all environmental submissions are robust, credible, and capable of withstanding external scrutiny.
• Navigate evolving regulatory frameworks associated with emerging fusion technologies.
• Drive continuous improvement through lessons learned from environmental performance and regulatory engagement.
Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement
• Act as a senior ambassador for environmental and sustainability performance across the organisation.
• Influence programme teams, supply chain partners, contractors, and external stakeholders.
• Represent the organisation confidently with regulators, government bodies, local communities, and industry partners.
• Champion a culture where environmental responsibility and sustainability are recognised as critical to engineering excellence and programme success.
• Foster an inclusive, collaborative, and high-performing team environment.
About You
We're looking for a strategic environmental leader with experience delivering complex, highly regulated infrastructure, energy, nuclear, environmental, or major capital programmes.
Essential Experience
• Significant leadership experience in environmental and sustainability management within a regulated industry.
• Proven track record of developing and delivering environmental strategies for major infrastructure, energy, nuclear, industrial, or engineering programmes.
• Experience leading environmental consenting, permitting, and regulatory engagement activities.
• Strong understanding of environmental impact assessment methodologies, environmental management systems, and environmental risk management.
• Experience integrating environmental requirements within major engineering, construction, or operational projects.
• Demonstrated capability in leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing senior stakeholders.
• Expertise in environmental governance, assurance, and programme-level decision making.
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including engagement with regulators and government bodies.
Desirable Experience
• Experience supporting Development Consent Orders (DCOs) and nationally significant infrastructure projects.
• Knowledge of radiological and non-radiological waste management principles.
• Understanding of Best Available Techniques (BAT) assessments.
• Experience within the nuclear, fusion, energy generation, or similarly regulated sectors.
• Chartered environmental, engineering, sustainability, or related professional status.
What You'll Bring
• Strategic thinking and commercial awareness.
• Outstanding leadership and influencing skills.
• Technical credibility combined with pragmatic decision-making.
• The ability to navigate complexity and ambiguity with confidence.
• A passion for environmental stewardship and sustainable innovation.
• Curiosity, resilience, and a commitment to continuous improvement.
Why Join Us?
This is an opportunity to help create a new energy industry while shaping the environmental standards that will define it.
You will work alongside world-leading scientists, engineers, regulators, and policymakers to ensure fusion energy is developed responsibly and sustainably.
Join us and help deliver clean energy for generations to come.

Qualifications
Essential:
• Degree or equivalent in a relevant subject, environmental engineering or related field.
• Proven extensive experience in the environmental discipline, having worked with large programmes of similar complexity.
• Expert understanding of environmental and sustainability legislation and standards.

• A strong understanding of ISO14001 standard &/or other environmental management frameworks including experience in the certification process.

About This Job
As Lead Product Manager, you will lead and own the R&D Activity Product-Oriented Delivery (POD) within CP R&D IT. You will be accountable for a portfolio of digital products that enable R&D innovation across both laboratory and field environments.
You will shape the POD vision and multi-horizon roadmap, make prioritisation and investment decisions, define clear product boundaries, and drive measurable improvements in how R&D captures, manages, and uses data—from laboratory experimentation and assay workflows to field trials, sensors, imaging, and geospatial data.
This is a senior product leadership role. You will lead a cross-functional team and may line-manage and develop Product Managers within the POD, ensuring scalable, sustainable, secure, and high-quality digital products with clear business outcomes.
Key responsibilities
• Co-create the POD vision, value hypotheses, and multi-horizon product roadmap with business and technical stakeholders.
• Translate strategy into a coherent product portfolio aligned with business priorities, investment decisions, and enterprise architecture.
• Define product boundaries, ownership, taxonomy, interfaces, and dependencies across PODs.
• Establish and track POD-level success measures, including OKRs, KPIs, adoption, user outcomes, operational performance, value realisation, and total cost of ownership.
• Act as the senior voice of the customer, ensuring enterprise and user needs are understood, validated, and reflected in product direction.
• Lead stakeholder engagement across R&D, business, IT, data, security, architecture, quality, and compliance functions.
• Own product delivery governance, prioritisation cadence, backlog health, release planning, capacity allocation, and management of scope, time, cost, and value trade-offs.
• Drive operational excellence through reliable product operations, incident and problem management, root-cause analysis, and post-launch value tracking.
• Manage POD-level risks, dependencies, data governance, security, regulatory constraints, and vendor or partner relationships.
• Ensure data solutions align with FAIR principles, data quality, traceability, provenance, auditability, metadata, and standardisation requirements.
• Partner with technical leads and architects to deliver scalable, reusable, secure, and enterprise-aligned solutions.
• Monitor relevant market trends and emerging technologies across lab and field R&D, including LIMS/ELN, lab automation, instrument connectivity, mobile/offline solutions, IoT and sensors, geospatial/GIS, imaging, and digital phenotyping.
• Lead, coach, and develop Product Managers, strengthening product practice and delivery capability across the POD.
• Manage POD budget allocation, resource planning, and financial performance, ensuring optimal return on investment and cost-effective delivery of digital solutions.
• Establish regular stakeholder communication cadences and reporting mechanisms to maintain transparency on product progress, risks, and business impact across the organisation.
• Leverage product analytics and data-driven insights to inform prioritisation decisions, validate product hypotheses, and continuously optimise user experience and business outcomes.

Qualifications
**Required:**
• Demonstrated experience leading product-centric, cross-functional teams and delivering measurable outcomes through Agile and Lean product practices.
• Strong product strategy skills, including vision setting, roadmap development, prioritisation, portfolio management, and value measurement through OKRs/KPIs.
• Experience managing complex digital product portfolios in enterprise environments.
• Understanding of digital R&D workflows in laboratory and/or field environments, including data capture, experimentation, trial execution, automation, sensors, imaging, geospatial data, and data standards.
• Knowledge of data integrity, discoverability, metadata, taxonomy/ontology, traceability, provenance, auditability, and quality controls across data pipelines.
• Experience working with data governance, security, architecture, quality, compliance, and regulatory requirements.
• Strong stakeholder management and change leadership skills, with the ability to influence without formal authority.
• Ability to navigate ambiguity, make sound trade-offs, and communicate effectively with business and technical leaders.
• Strategic and systems-thinking mindset, with the ability to simplify complex challenges whilst maintaining end-to-end design integrity.
• Bachelor's or advanced degree in IT, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience.
**Preferred:**
• Proven experience in product analytics, data-driven decision-making, and continuous optimisation of user experience and business outcomes.
• Demonstrated capability in budget allocation, resource planning, and financial performance management to ensure optimal return on investment.
• Experience managing vendor relationships, third-party integrations, and partner collaborations within complex technology environments.
• Knowledge of incident and problem management frameworks, root-cause analysis methodologies, and post-launch value tracking processes.
• Familiarity with FAIR principles (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability) and industry-standard data frameworks relevant to R&D environments.
**What will make you successful**
You are a collaborative, curious, and value-oriented leader who sees digital technology as an enabler of meaningful R&D and business outcomes. You are comfortable operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment, balancing strategic ambition with delivery discipline, and bringing diverse teams together around a shared product vision.

Do you want to help people in need and make a difference in their lives? Do you want to work with the elderly, but don't have any experience or qualifications? If so, then becoming a care assistant might be your perfect career.
As someone who cares for others on a daily basis, we know that it can bring huge rewards. And when we say ‘rewarding’, we’re not just talking about pay. As a care assistant, you can make a real difference to the lives of older adults in your local area by giving them the support they need to live independently in their own homes.
Care Assistant Pay & Benefits
•
Flexible Hours Available - 16-20 Hours Per Week
•
Industry-Leading Training
•
Full PPE Protection
•
Care Certification
•
Employee Benefit Scheme
•
Career Development & Progression Opportunities
Becoming a Care Assistant
As one of our care assistants, you’ll be earning minimum £13.36 per hour with industry-leading training and support provided.
You will be required to work alternative weekends and due to the nature of the role, you will need a full UK driving license & access to reliable transportation to visit your clients.
No specific qualifications or background in care is required to become a care assistant. What’s more important is that you have a natural calling to care for people. With this intact, we provide all the training you need o to become one of our exceptional Home Instead CAREGivers.
As well as supporting older adults within their communities, we support employees by providing opportunities such as advanced industry-leading training, employment opportunities & benefits schemes.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join our award-winning, small, family-run, local home care company whose visits always involve a strong element of companionship.
Care Assistant Job Description
This is a totally unique care sector opportunity - We will carefully match you to your own small circle of older adults in your local community and you will support them to live happy, independent lives by providing:
•
Prompting & assisting your clients with their medication
•
Support getting in & out of the shower & getting dressed
•
Help to & from the loo
•
Preparing simple meals and light household duties
•
Companionship, a cup of tea & a natter
•
Shopping tips, social Calls, appointments, clubs hobbies (own car advantageous)

•
Flexible Part-time hours are available between 16-20 hours per week (unfortunately, we cannot offer purely school hours or full-time as each employee only has a small circle of their own regular clients)

If you have some availability mornings (ideally starting at 8:00) or tea/evening times (ideally starting at 17:00) & a couple of hours alternate weekends, then this position could fit around your other interests & commitments
•
Excellent training is provided and you’ll meet some like-minded people
•
The biggest benefit of all is making a difference every day and putting a smile on your client’s faces

About This Job
Forget everything you think you know about working in care. We do it differently!
Our hours are flexible and we have no calls under 1 hour. Calls are very often 2/3/4 hours long. You don’t get a schedule that changes every week, you will be allocated clients that match your availability and continue to care for those same clients each week.
We don't just do personal care, we do everything for our clients that you would do for your own loved ones.
Experience is not necessary. We believe in our training not experience. We offer excellent rates of pay and benefits as well as our accredited training developing your talent for caring.
What we can offer you:
• Our calls last a minimum of 1 hour so you can build strong relationships.
• Full training and development.
• No pressure between client visits.
• Excellent pay rates, holiday pay, pension, mileage and employer benefits including Employee Assistance Programme.
What we need from you:
• You must have your own transport available.
• You have availability that covers at least 4 days each week.
• You are willing to help clients with personal care, home help and companionship.
The only skills you need are to be caring and compassionate. So if you are looking for part-time work during daytime, evenings and/or weekends get in touch.

Kitchen Operations

• Ensure smooth communication between kitchen and front-of-house teams
Team Leadership

• Conduct performance reviews and ongoing training

Stock & Cost Control

• Minimise waste and control kitchen costs effectively
• Monitor gross profit margins and labour percentages
• Complete regular stock takes and maintain accurate records

• Share of tips
• Staff meals whilst on duty
• Supportive leadership team and positive working environment
• Staff discounts and employee benefits

• Ensuring that designs maximise sustainability outcomes during construction and over whole life of assets;

About This Job
QIMA’s rapid growth has added complexity in data, systems, processes, and management structures. Successful integration requires close collaboration between technical, commercial, and core business teams. This role is responsible for driving that collaboration.
The Technical Project Manager, Commercial Integrations is an individual contributor responsible for the end-to-end integration of data, systems, and operational processes from acquired companies into QIMA's core infrastructure. You will own workstreams from initial data discovery and process mapping, through to production-ready pipelines and process handover, coordinating across legal, finance, commercial, and technical stakeholders. This is a mid-level role requiring engineering rigour and commercial fluency in equal measure: genuinely at home with data, and equally able to explain what you are doing and why it matters to people who will never open a database.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Project Management
• Own project plans, timelines, risk registers, and status reporting for all active integration workstreams; escalate blockers and business decisions proactively.
• Maintain integration documentation, decision logs, and handover notes that enable teams to own the output once integration is complete.
Stakeholder Management & Communication
• Coordinate across Legal, IT, Finance, Sales, Marketing, and Revenue Operations to gather requirements, identify dependencies and handoffs, secure milestone sign-off, and manage competing priorities.
• Translate complex data processes into clear, accessible language for non-technical stakeholders at all seniority levels.
M&A Data Integration
• Lead post-acquisition data integration workstreams: discovery, profiling, schema mapping, matching, cleansing, and migration from acquired entities into QIMA systems.
• Define integration plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria; identify data quality or process issues early and drive well communicated remediations.
• Validate data integrity across source and target systems at each stage; facilitate knowledge-extraction with acquired company experts before systems are decommissioned.
Data Engineering & Automation
• Build or coordinate data pipelines and ETL processes; apply AI and machine learning tooling to accelerate data ingestion, deduplication, and anomaly detection.
• Design automated quality checks that reduce manual validation effort without compromising accuracy.
Master Data Management & Governance
• Apply MDM principles to align acquired data with QIMA master data standards; define ownership, stewardship rules, and lineage documentation for integrated datasets.
• Navigate data protection and privacy requirements throughout integration, ensuring GDPR compliance while preserving data usability for analytics and AI applications.

Qualifications
Required Experience
• 5-7 years in technical project management, including data integration or data engineering, with proven track record delivering complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
• Hands-on experience with schema mapping, data matching and deduplication, ETL design, and data quality validation.
• Working knowledge of SQL; Python or comparable scripting for data processing and automation.
• Understanding of MDM concepts (data domains, golden records, ownership, lineage) and PII regulations (GDPR and equivalent), including the practical balance between compliance and AI usability.
• Experience managing project workstreams across multiple concurrent stakeholder groups spanning commercial and technical functions.
• Exceptional English-language communication skills with proven ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences in writing and in meetings.
• Bonus: post-merger integration experience, including direct exposure to CRM, marketing automation, or ERP systems in a data integration capacity
• Bonus: project management certification (PMP, Prince2, or Agile/Scrum).
Desired Characteristics
• Clear Communicator: You can make a data mapping discussion accessible to a CFO and credible to a data engineer, and you know which version to use in which room.
• Disciplined with Detail: Integration work lives and dies in the detail. You catch discrepancies before they reach production and document decisions so they are not repeated.
• Technically Grounded, Commercially Aware: You understand data architecture and frame technical work in terms of the outcomes it enables.
• Comfortable with Ambiguity: Acquired data is rarely clean and processes are rarely documented. You impose structure and clarity without being rigid.
• Collaborative by Default: You coordinate large, cross-functional groups without a reporting line through preparation, clarity, and trust.

Additional Information
Does this describe you? Then we want to hear from you as soon as possible! Apply now with your CV in English and we can write the next chapter of the QIMA story together!

Join Ramboll’s UK Healthcare team as a Principal Electrical Engineer and lead electrical engineering design and advisory for technically demanding hospital and healthcare projects across the UK and internationally. We’re looking for someone with a proven track record delivering electrical building services on complex healthcare or high‑resilience projects, strong digital design capability, and either chartered status or qualifications that support MCIBSE, MIET or MIHEEM membership — with Ramboll providing structured chartership and professional development support. If you’re passionate about innovative engineering that improves patient care and advances sustainable outcomes, this role offers the scope to make a real impact.
Your new role
As Principal Electrical Engineer in Ramboll’s UK Healthcare team you’ll provide senior technical leadership on a portfolio of technically demanding hospital and healthcare projects across the UK and internationally. You’ll combine hands‑on design and review with client engagement, team mentoring and project delivery responsibility to shape resilient, low‑carbon electrical strategies and ensure excellent digital delivery.
We offer flexible working arrangements with candidates able to work from any of our primary offices as well as home. We have an exciting range of ongoing projects including Hillerød Hospital Denmark, Cambridge Children’s Hospital, Kettering General Hospital and KEMH, Falklands Islands.
Key responsibilities
• Provide senior technical leadership for electrical building services from concept through to handover.
• Support and mentor the electrical team (engineers and technicians) and coordinate with multi‑disciplinary colleagues (mechanical, structural, public health, etc.).
• Develop and oversee electrical design concepts and detailed design, producing and reviewing calculations, specifications and drawings to meet UK healthcare standards.
• Lead digital delivery and MEP coordination using Revit (BIM 360) and industry tools (e.g., MagiCad, Dialux, IES, Trimble).
• Act as a client‑facing technical lead: present solutions, chair technical workshops and maintain strong client relationships.
• Manage project scope, resource allocation and delivery as electrical/MEP project manager, identifying and mitigating technical and commercial risks.
• Embed best practice in sustainability, resilience and quality assurance across projects.
• Enhance Ramboll’s profile by contributing to proposals, technical thought leadership and external stakeholder engagement.
Your new team
You’ll join a growing, national Healthcare team delivering an ambitious five‑year strategy. Our multidisciplinary group works across long‑term programmes and high‑profile new‑build acute hospitals, delivering projects that improve patient care and support NHS services.

• Meaningful impact: work on projects that directly benefit patients, staff and communities.
• Broad portfolio: national and international projects, from estate renewals to large hospital new builds.
• Collaborative culture: partner with leading UK and international architects and multidisciplinary specialists in a design‑driven environment rooted in strong Scandinavian design values.
• Career progression: clear development pathways, chartership support and opportunities to grow technically or into client/project leadership.
• Flexible ways of working: national footprint with the option to be based at any UK office and hybrid working as standard.

• Demonstrable track record delivering electrical building services on UK projects — ideally healthcare or other high‑resilience/technically complex schemes.
• Proven technical or project leadership with experience mentoring engineers and driving a collaborative, inclusive culture.
• Degree (or equivalent) in electrical, building services or related engineering discipline.
• Eligibility for, or progress towards, corporate membership (MCIBSE, MIET or MIHEEM) — Ramboll provides chartership support.
• Strong competence in digital design delivery (Revit/BIM 360) and familiarity with MEP analysis/design tools (e.g., MagiCad, Dialux, IES, Trimble).
• Excellent project management skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and to identify and mitigate technical and commercial risks.
• Clear, confident communicator able to explain complex technical concepts to clients and multidisciplinary teams, verbally and in writing.
• Self‑starter who can work autonomously across technical aspects of the discipline while building client relationships.
We welcome applicants from different career stages. If you don’t meet every bullet but have the right aptitude and passion, please apply — we value potential and will support your development.
We’ll support your professional development and chartership, and we’re looking for a senior electrical engineer who can lead technical delivery and client engagement on complex healthcare projects.

About This Job
About the Role
AECOM is looking for talented and motivated graduates to join our Traffic Engineering teams across the UK and Ireland (UK&I). As one of the largest dedicated Traffic Engineering teams in the UK&I, we work on a diverse range of projects focused on creating safer, more efficient and sustainable transport networks for communities.
Our work covers the development and appraisal of practical solutions for pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles, including road and street design, traffic signals, cycle facilities, traffic management and traffic modelling. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and other technical professionals in multidisciplinary teams to develop innovative, cost-effective solutions for our clients.
Projects range from concept and preliminary design through to modelling, detailed design and implementation, giving you the opportunity to gain experience across the full project lifecycle. The role is fast-paced and collaborative, requiring creativity, technical capability, strong communication and a willingness to learn.
What You’ll Do
As a Graduate Traffic Engineer, you’ll be supported by experienced engineers who will provide guidance and mentoring as you develop your technical knowledge and professional skills. You’ll work on live projects and receive structured training to help you build a strong foundation in traffic engineering and design.
Your initial responsibilities will typically include supporting the development of designs and technical solutions through different project stages, attending site visits, meetings and workshops, and working collaboratively with clients and other design professionals.

About This Job
About the Role
We are looking for a driven Aerodynamics Project Leader to work closely with our Principal Aerodynamicists and take the technical lead of a team of talented engineers. You will own aerodynamic development projects from first concept through to track validation, turning a clear performance objective into a released, manufactured and correlated solution on the car.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will set the direction for your project team, make the calls on where to focus limited CFD and wind tunnel resource, and keep a development programme moving at race-team pace while protecting quality and learning. Just as importantly, you will develop and empower the engineers around you, creating an environment where ideas are challenged openly and the best solution wins.
Working within the constraints of the FIA regulations and the cost cap, you will need to be as smart with your resource as you are with your geometry. Every run, every tunnel hour and every release has to count!
Responsibilities
You will take a project from the first spark of an idea to a part running on the car, turning performance targets into clear objectives and building plans that balance CFD, wind tunnel time, design office capacity and manufacturing lead times against the race calendar. Spotting risks early and dealing with them before they become problems will be second nature.
Day to day, you will:
• Lead concept generation, challenge assumptions about how the car works, and direct CFD exploration with evidence-based decisions on what to pursue and what to park
• Plan and run test sessions in our onsite wind tunnel, analyse results with rigour, and adjust course when the data tells a different story
• Get hands-on in CAD where needed to develop and refine aerodynamic surfaces
• Drive projects through release, working closely with the Design Office, Structures, Composites and Manufacturing teams to protect aerodynamic intent within weight, stiffness, cost and build constraints
• Support the introduction of new parts at the track alongside Vehicle Performance and trackside engineers
Just as importantly, you will bring the project team with you. You will communicate results and theories clearly in a way that encourages challenge, coach and empower less experienced engineers through delegation and honest feedback, and lead post-project reviews so we learn from what worked and what did not. You will also help shape a culture of continuous improvement in our tools, methods and processes.
About You
You are an experienced F1 aerodynamicist who has taken technical projects the whole way from concept to track. You understand the fundamentals well enough to explain the flow physics behind a result, not just the number, and you are comfortable making and defending a decision when the data is incomplete and the clock is ticking.
You will bring:
• Multiple years’ experience in F1 aerodynamic development
• Demonstrable experience leading projects through the full aero development lifecycle, from concept to track
• Familiarity with CFD techniques, including non-standard models
• Experience planning and running wind tunnel programmes, and interpreting CFD, tunnel and track correlation
• A strong working understanding of the ATR and cost cap framework
• Proficiency in CAD for aerodynamic surfaces (preferably NX)
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to develop less experienced team members

Additional Information

• Coachability and genuine drive to develop — you want to be challenged, not just comfortable

About This Job
We are providing free high quality training, recognised to the national standard of The Care Certificate, for those who would like to join Home instead as a CAREGiver. No experience within the care sector is needed.
Why are we providing this incentive?
We have had unrivalled enquires from potential Clients wanting CAREGivers to support them to stay independent at home. This may have something to do with our recent TV sponsorship with Alan Titchmarsh's gardening programme!
We are looking for caring and compassionate people to become part of our expanding team to help the Older Adults,  within B74 and B75 postcode area, to retain their choice and control over how and where they want to live. To help them start their day by supporting them with their morning routine, breakfast and if required medication. Or perhaps ensure that the Client is supported with their evening routine to ensure they have safely gone to bed.
CAREGivers work part time, mornings or evenings and most definitely alternate weekends. This role can be fitted around your own commitments.
Our CAREGivers are matched to the Clients and then visit them consistently allowing CAREGivers to see the difference they are making to their lives.
Our CAREGivers visit a Client for a minimum of 1 hour or more……………we do not do 15 minute calls or even half hour calls.
Our CAREGivers travel locally (within 15 minutes of own postcode) to visit their Clients. We work with Clients within their own homes. You will therefore need a car to travel from one Clients home to another Clients home.
Our employed CAREGivers are important to  us and we believe that when you join us you become part of the Home Instead family.
What CAREGivers can expect from Home Instead;
·         CAREGiving hourly rate up to £15.75 per hour
·         Waiting and travel time £8.91 per hour
·         Mileage paid at 23p per mile
·         Free DBS check
·         Enhanced CAREGiving hourly rate for bank holiday visits
·         Contributions to a company Pension (after qualifying hours)
·         Free membership providing cash back for vital health benefits
·         Free Membership to Shopping discounts
·         Free Employee Assistant programme helping with personal and life challenges
·         Paid monthly training
·         Paid quarterly supervisions
·         Quarterly social events for CAREGivers
·         Regular business updates and communication
·         Appreciation gifts and awards
·         Supportive environment
·         Professional environment
·         Fun place to work
*To qualify for the £400 payment CAREGivers must have worked a minimum of 40 hours. If a Caregiver terminates within 6 months of payment, the £400 will be required to be paid back. Once the Care Certificate is attained, the hourly CARE Giving rate will be £10.40.

About This Job
About the role
We’re looking for an Engineering Operations Manager with previous SOX experience to lead large-scale engineering programmes and support engineering tribes with planning, coordination and operational improvements.
You’ll bring structure to complex programmes spanning multiple teams, turn broad priorities into clear delivery plans and help stakeholders resolve risks and dependencies. Alongside this broader remit, you’ll help engineering teams translate SOX requirements into coordinated action and establish sustainable ways of managing their control responsibilities.
This role suits someone who combines strong programme management with a practical, hands-on approach. You’ll be comfortable leading cross-functional initiatives, managing different stakeholders, partnering with engineering leaders and working through the operational details that keep programmes moving.
How we work
You’ll join a small Engineering Operations team, working across engineering and business functions. We bring clarity to complex work through practical planning, clear ownership and consistent follow-through.
You’ll partner with tribe leadership to strengthen planning and operational reviews, while working with control owners and colleagues in Risk, Compliance and Audit on SOX-related activities. You’ll coordinate delivery and provide visibility, with engineering teams and control owners retaining responsibility for technical decisions, control execution and evidence.
What you’ll achieve
•
Lead large-scale engineering programmes. Define outcomes, scope, workstreams and milestones, coordinating delivery across teams from initial planning through to ongoing operations
•
Provide tribe-level Engineering Operations support. Partner with engineering leaders to strengthen planning, prioritisation, operational reviews and follow-through on commitments
•
Coordinate SOX and IT General Controls audits . Bring structure to remediation planning, testing readiness and the transition from project completion to repeatable operational processes
•
Manage risks and dependencies. Identify blockers early, clarify ownership and help stakeholders resolve competing priorities and decisions that affect delivery
•
Build clear governance and reporting. Give stakeholders a dependable view of programme progress, remediation across teams and testing outcomes. Drive action and decision follow-through. Maintain clear accountability, escalate issues with their impact and help teams agree practical next steps
•
Drives framework and owns internal training, awareness & communication.
•
Improve operational processes. Use data and automation to reduce manual reporting and coordination, and make programme information easier to maintain and use
•
Establish sustainable handovers. Ensure ongoing responsibilities, processes and ownership are clear when programmes move into business-as-usual operations.
What you’ll bring
•
A strong track record of independently leading large-scale technology programmes involving multiple teams and business functions
•
Previous hands-on experience managing SOX or IT General Controls programmes, including coordinating engineering teams through remediation, testing or audit cycles
•
An understanding of control ownership, evidence requirements and the distinction between implementing a change and having it validated for closure.
•
Experience translating regulatory or audit requirements into practical delivery plans with technical and control specialists
•
Experience working closely with engineering leaders on planning, priorities, dependencies and operational improvements
•
The ability to turn ambiguous problems into clear plans and drive progress without relying on formal authority
•
Strong stakeholder management and the confidence to challenge unclear ownership, incomplete plans and unsupported progress claims
•
Clear communication, including the ability to facilitate difficult discussions and give leaders concise updates on progress, risks and decisions
•
An analytical approach, with experience using data to identify problems, assess progress and improve ways of working
Previous SOX or ITGC programme experience is important for this role. You don’t need to meet every other requirement: if you bring relevant experience and are eager to develop further, we’d love to hear from you.

Additional Information
£92,000-£118,000k
For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ifs1/7440001426.description_excerpt:
About This Job
You'll be designing for people whose work actually matters: maintenance engineers, field service technicians, operations planners working in environments where the software either helps or gets in the way. The stakes are real and the problems are hard, which is exactly what makes this role interesting.
At IFS, product design means owning the full problem, not just the screens. You'll work in a cross-functional squad alongside engineers and product managers, with the scope and support to do the work properly. From problem framing through to something shipped and measured.
But the deeper question is harder than that. The industries IFS serves (field service, asset management, manufacturing, supply chain) are changing faster than the software that runs them. By 2030, we're not confident the interface paradigms we rely on today will still be the right ones. AI, ambient computing, voice, autonomous systems: any of these could fundamentally change how an operations planner or a field engineer interacts with software, or whether they interact with it at all.
That's not a problem we've solved. It's the problem you'd be working on.
What you'll do
Product Design
•
Own design for defined feature areas end-to-end — from problem framing through to production-ready Figma files, with a clear rationale for every decision
•
Work in a cross-functional squad with engineers and PMs, making real decisions rather than executing on someone else's brief
•
Present design thinking to stakeholders with confidence — handling pushback with evidence, not just conviction
Discovery & Research
•
Plan and run user interviews, JTBD analysis, and journey mapping independently — turning findings into clear design direction, not just a readout
•
Track quantitative signals alongside qualitative insight, and use both to drive iteration
AI & Emerging Technology
•
Design AI-driven features with a clear understanding of where AI helps and where it introduces risk — prompts, fallbacks, and human-in-the-loop moments included
•
Bring a genuine perspective on how the interfaces we're building today might become obsolete — and what should replace them
Design Systems & Quality
•
Contribute to the IFS design system by proposing reusable components and patterns rather than designing one-offs
•
Apply WCAG 2.1+ accessibility standards from the start, and design for edge cases, error states, and real-world data — not just the happy path
You'll know it's working when your work ships, holds up in the field, and raises the bar for the next thing. Concretely: task success rates improve, UX-related support tickets drop, and the squad reaches for your work as a reference rather than a starting point.

Qualifications
You may be a good fit if you:
•
You have at least eight years of end-to-end product design experience — from discovery through to shipped product — and you can point to work that reflects real ownership, not just execution
•
You're comfortable running your own research: planning the study, conducting interviews, synthesising findings, and turning them into a clear design direction
•
You know how to work in a cross-functional squad — making real decisions alongside engineers and PMs, not waiting to be handed a brief
•
You know Figma well and have the visual craft to back your thinking up
•
You treat accessibility as a design constraint from the start, not a checklist at the end
•
You've thought seriously about what AI means for the interfaces you build — not just as a feature to add, but as something that changes the fundamental design problem
•
You measure your work — task success rates, support ticket volume, adoption — and use those signals to drive the next iteration
Strong candidates may also have:
•
Experience shipping AI-driven features — prompts, fallbacks, human-in-the-loop moments — not just awareness of the concepts
•
Familiarity with design tokens, contribution models, and what it means to design for a system rather than a screen
•
Some exposure to quantitative signals: task success rates, funnel data, or A/B results — and a habit of using them

Additional Information
We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

This senior level professional possesses exceptional technical, presentation, consulting, and communication skills, enabling strategic customers to assess their current cryptographic environments, understand modernization opportunities, and develop practical adoption strategies that align with their security, compliance, and business objectives.
This is a full-time, remote role, and we’re ideally looking for someone based in the greater London area. • Act as a trusted strategic advisor to CISOs, enterprise architects, PKI administrators, security teams, and executive stakeholders, guiding customers through cryptographic modernization and quantum readiness initiatives.
• Partner with regional Sales Engineers and Account Executives to identify, develop, and support strategic opportunities involving cryptographic modernization, Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM), Private PKI, and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).

• Conduct cryptographic and quantum readiness assessments, helping customers identify risks, prioritize modernization efforts, and develop practical migration strategies.

• Lead Proof of Concept (PoC) engagements by planning, deploying, configuring, implementing, and validating Sectigo solutions within customer environments.
• Perform hands-on implementation activities including deployment of discovery technologies, technical integrations, connector configuration, and validation as required during customer engagements.
• Bridge the gap between technology and business objectives by helping customers understand the value of cryptographic modernization, Certificate Lifecycle Management, and machine identity security.
• Assist with sales proposals, Statements of Work (SOWs), Requests for Proposal (RFPs), and Requests for Information (RFIs), ensuring technical accuracy and competitive differentiation.
• Develop and refine repeatable methodologies, assessment frameworks, technical playbooks, reference architectures, and best practices supporting Sectigo's cryptographic modernization practice.
• Contribute to the SE Readiness Program by developing subject matter expertise, sharing technical best practices, maintaining current knowledge of assigned solutions, and delivering technical enablement to the field organization.
• Work closely with Product Management and Engineering, providing field-driven feedback to influence future product capabilities, customer experience, and solution strategy.
• Collaborate with Product Marketing, Customer Success, Professional Services, and Strategic Alliances to support solution adoption, partner enablement, and customer success.
• Represent Sectigo as a technical thought leader by participating in customer workshops, executive briefings, conferences, webinars, industry events, and technical content development.

• Willing to travel regionally and internationally for customer-facing activities, strategic partner engagements, conferences, and internal planning sessions.

• Microsoft Certified Professional (considered an asset).
• Linux/Solaris/UNIX System Administration (considered an asset).
• Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud certification (considered an asset).
• Security, PKI, or cryptography-related certifications (considered an asset).
Experience:
• Minimum of 7+ years of industry experience, with at least 3-4 years in an enterprise pre-sales environment.
• Proven experience as a Sales Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Security Architect, or Professional Services Engineer supporting enterprise security, identity, or cloud solutions.
• Strong knowledge of Microsoft Active Directory, Windows Server platforms, Linux environments, and enterprise authentication technologies.
• Extensive experience with Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM), including automated certificate issuance, renewal, revocation, and lifecycle automation.
• Expertise establishing and managing Private PKI environments, including Certificate Authorities (CAs), enterprise trust models, and PKI integrations.
• Deep understanding of Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), SSL/TLS, X.509 certificates, digital identity, cryptographic principles, and machine identity management.
• Strong understanding of cryptographic algorithms, key management, Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), digital signatures, and enterprise trust architectures.
• Working knowledge of cryptographic modernization, crypto-agility principles, and Post-Quantum Cryptography concepts is highly desirable.
• Experience conducting enterprise technical discovery, architecture assessments, and solution design for complex customer environments.
• Hands-on experience deploying, configuring, integrating, and validating enterprise security solutions.
• Strong cloud experience with Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud (preferred).
• Proficiency with scripting languages (PowerShell, Python, Bash) and REST APIs (preferred).

About This Job
Self-employed / No-contract / Temporary / Part-time / Shift-work
https://flex.amazon.co.uk/recruiting-cities/london per hour* based on delivering a number of parcels across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block).
Deliveries will be collected from the depot in Wimbledon and will be made to the surrounding areas.
Deliver packages locally and get paid weekly. Flexible hours. Be your own boss.
What is Amazon Flex?
It's simple! You use your own vehicle and your smartphone to deliver packages locally for Amazon as a way of earning extra money weekly to move you closer to your goals. Schedule a delivery block and start delivering parcels as little or as often as you like.
Who can deliver for Amazon Flex?
To become a Delivery Driver you need a valid UK driving licence and a vehicle. Currently the only available delivery options are for owners of a 4-door car or van.You will need to be entitled to work in the UK and pass a background and criminal record check which includes, but is not limited to, a review of driving licence records. Current Amazon employees are not eligible to be Delivery Partners.
How do I sign up?
Grab your mobile and visit the Amazon Flex website to download the app for iPhone or Android. After the download, the app guides you step-by-step through the onboarding process. Once you have passed your background and criminal record check, you will be able to schedule a block and start delivering smiles!
How long are the blocks?
Blocks vary in length, from 1 to 5 hours, depending on the delivery service you support. For example, 1-hour and 2-hour blocks are available for Prime Now deliveries, where customers receive their deliveries within a few hours of making their order. However, for https://www.amazon.co.uk/ deliveries, the area served is larger. In those cases, it's not feasible to have 1-hour or 2-hour blocks and the available blocks are 4-hour and 5-hour.
Money Matters. Know your earnings.
When you schedule a delivery block, you'll know estimated duration and your total payments all before your delivery block begins. You can build your own schedule, there are delivery blocks available seven days a week. However, the available delivery blocks may fluctuate week-to-week and are not guaranteed.
Adjust your work not your life.
Perhaps you have a job but want to supplement your income. Or maybe you are already a delivery driver and want something to keep you busy on the quieter days. Whatever your situation Amazon Flex can offer you the freedom and flexibility to be your own boss and earn extra cash on your own schedule.
No matter what drives you, Amazon Flex helps you get there. Sign-up today.
* Earnings estimates are based on delivering a number of packages across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block), completed while driving a standard motorised vehicle. Should Amazon Flex introduce blocks eligible to be delivered using scooters or other alternative modes of transportation, different rates may apply. We aim to ensure that the number of packages you are assigned to deliver within your block is realistic, taking into account congestion and the primary requirement to drive safely.

About This Job
Are you an experienced environmental due diligence consultant, skilled in uncovering environmental risks and turning technical findings into clear, actionable advice for decision-makers? Do you enjoy working across EHS and ESG topics to help shape sustainable outcomes for transactions and post-acquisition strategies? Are you a detail-focused communicator who thrives on fast-paced due diligence work, site visits, and collaborative problem-solving?
If this sounds like you, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our CST Due Diligence UK & Ireland team as our new Experienced Senior Consultant Environmental Due Diligence and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.
Your new role
As an Experienced Senior Consultant Environmental Due Diligence, you will be part of our busy UK transactions team supporting fast-paced UK and global M&A transactions. You will assist with the identification of key EHS and ESG risks and opportunities and provide high-quality, targeted advice to clients on both buy-side and sell-side due diligence projects
Our team advises on transactions across a wide range of sectors, typically including industrial, commercial and infrastructure assets and businesses, often for finance sector clients. We work closely with in-house specialists across several EHS and ESG disciplines to provide targeted due diligence advice. Our clients use this advice to support negotiations during the bidding process and o to make informed impactful decisions on sustainability priorities post-acquisition.
You will play a key role in the team, principally delivering due diligence assessments, while also supporting project management and the development of client proposals.
Your key responsibilities will be:
• Preparation of proposals, including pricing/budgets and timescales. Participation in client discussions and support with developing new client relationships.
• Project Management and coordination of medium to large projects including multi-site projects over several geographies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence.
• Delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments and Limited Environmental Compliance Review(LECR) assessments for a range of sites, including more complex manufacturing facilities; including participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing focussed client reports.
• Delivery of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) assessments of companies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence. This will include desk-based research (review of data rooms and publicly available information), participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing client focussed reports.
About you
If you have relevant EHS/ESG knowledge, experience in due diligence and want to advance your career in a collaborative team, we would like to hear from you.What matters most to us:
• Relevant degree/qualifications. Ideally in environmental studies/geography or similar.
• Sound understanding of UK environmental regulations and an understanding of key environmental and sustainability regulations in Europe.
• 7 to 12 years of practical work experience in other companies where you have personally been involved in the delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments, LECR assessments, ideally including to ASTM standards, and ideally also ESG assessments. Have the ability to understand information quickly and work efficiently, proactively and autonomously.
• Experience in supporting the preparation of proposals.
• Strong communication skills (both written and verbal), and be comfortable engaging with external clients and advisors.
• Project Management experience.
• A collaborative approach and willingness to travel, typically within the UK and Ireland.
What we can offer you
• Commitment to your development
• Leaders guided by our Leadership Principles
• A culture that welcomes you as the unique person you are
• Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
• The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company
• Flexible work environment
• 27 days annual leave plus bank holidays
• Matched pension contributions
• Private medical cover and life assurance
Ready to join us?
Please submit your application and CV online. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.
We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.
Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll
Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.
Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion
Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. Autonomy

• Where appropriate act as molecule lead on pipeline programmes, providing technical expertise and cross-functional leadership as teams form around assets

DJS-AbbVie is part of AbbVie Immunology and is focused on advancing novel therapeutics to address serious and challenging diseases. Our work is driven by scientific excellence, collaboration and a commitment to delivering meaningful impact for patients.

• Understanding of marketing data ecosystems including CDPs, CRM, marketing automation, digital behavioral data and journey orchestration.

An exciting opportunity to join our growing Neurology team
Following the continued growth and development of our Neurology service, alongside internal progression within the team, we are delighted to be looking to welcome an additional Referral Veterinary Nurse to our department. This is an exciting opportunity to join a well-established and supportive team and play an important role in the continued development of our neurology service.
Our Neurology team within the hospital currently consists of four neurology clinicians, one neurology intern, two neurology nurses and one neurology technician. The department is also supported by our anaesthesia and multidisciplinary nursing teams.
Your Role
Primarily as a neurology nurse, you will assist with consults, admits and discharges, nursing neurology patients, administering chemotherapy, and monitoring sedation and general anaesthesia for imaging, investigations and surgery.
We require all our associates to work closely with other hospital associates at all times to ensure efficient case throughput and gold standard patient and client experiences. All members of the nursing team are jointly responsible for maintaining high standards of hygiene, equipment care, effective stock control and rotation.
You will be encouraged to contribute to the continued growth of this service by sharing your valuable ideas and completing CPD according to your interests and development goals.
This is a great opportunity for an RVN with a keen interest in neurology to develop their understanding and practical abilities alongside our experienced and supportive team. The role provides exposure to a large and varied caseload and the opportunity to further develop your skills within a specialist referral environment.
You will have access to a wide range of internal CPD opportunities via Eastcott and Linnaeus, alongside a generous benefits package.
Referral experience is preferred but not essential, as full training will be provided.
Key responsibilities
• Preparing patients for anaesthesia, including patient examinations, administering premedication and assisting with induction.
• Monitoring patients undergoing anaesthesia for neurology investigations and procedures, including MRI, CT, neurosurgery and electro-diagnostics, under the supervision of the anaesthesia clinicians.
• Recovering patients from anaesthesia and handing over to ward nurses for further care.
• Preparing and sending cerebrospinal fluid samples for analysis to appropriate laboratories and assisting with cerebrospinal fluid collection.
• Providing inpatient care, including placement and maintenance of urinary catheters and administration of intravenous chemotherapy.
• Working alongside the physiotherapy team to assist with inpatient rehabilitation.
• Assisting with the creation of new protocols and SOPs relating to neurology and updating these as appropriate.
• Maintaining excellent lines of communication with the Workflow team to ensure patient flow across the hospital is efficient.

Staff discounts and benefits hub.

The Pipeline squad owns the infrastructure, build, release, and security foundations that every other Jetstream squad builds on top of. Jetstream is a NestJS + Angular monorepo deployed into Azure Kubernetes via Helm, shipped through GitLab CI/CD, and running on the wider PTC Atlas platform. We're the squad that makes shipping fast, safe, and boring so product squads can focus on features.
What you will do:
• Work on services from development through to deployment and running them in production.
• Build and maintain backend services, mainly using TypeScript, Node.js and NestJS.
• Help improve our GitLab CI/CD pipelines, including build, test, security and deployment.
• Work with Docker, Kubernetes and Helm to deploy and troubleshoot our services.
• Improve developer tooling and workflows, particularly where we can remove manual work or make things simpler.
• Help improve observability, monitoring and debugging across our services.
• Work alongside DevOps on infrastructure and automation where needed, including things like Terraform and Azure.
• Generally be comfortable working across backend development, CI/CD and the platform rather than focusing only on application code.
Experience:
• Strong backend development experience, ideally TypeScript/Node.js/NestJS.
• Good CI/CD experience, ideally GitLab CI.
• Good experience with Docker and some practical Kubernetes experience.
• Experience deploying and troubleshooting services, not just developing them locally.
• A good understanding of testing, debugging, logging and monitoring.
• Comfortable working across application and infrastructure/deployment areas.
• Helm, Terraform and Azure/AKS experience would be useful, but I wouldn't make all of these hard requirements.
• Experience with PostgreSQL, APIs and asynchronous/messaging systems would also be useful given the services we work with.
Nice to have:
• Experience creating agentic development workflows or writing and maintaining AI skills.
• npm workspaces / shared-package build systems.
• Experience supporting SaaS platforms with strict data-privacy requirements (enterprise/multinational customers).
How we work:
• We favor paved paths and sensible defaults over teams maintaining highly custom setups.
• Simplicitiy - the art of maximising the amount of work not done - is essential.
• Developers work end-to-end to solve customer problems, and our tooling encourages end-to-end workflows over platform components.
Life at PTC is about more than working with today’s most cutting-edge technologies to transform the physical world. It’s about showing up as you are and working alongside some of today’s most talented industry leaders to transform the world around you.
If you share our passion for problem-solving through innovation, you’ll likely become just as passionate about the PTC experience as we are. Are you ready to explore your next career move with us?

As a senior member of the team, you will provide strategic advice, oversee compliance delivery, manage multidisciplinary project teams, and support the continued growth of ERM’s post-consent services.
The Role
As a Consents Manager, you will lead environmental compliance and consent management activities throughout the post-consent phase of major projects. You will act as a trusted advisor to clients, ensuring that consent requirements, planning conditions, commitments, and legal obligations are effectively managed and discharged.
Key Responsibilities
•
Lead and deliver Environmental Consents Manager and Post-Consent Compliance Manager roles on major infrastructure projects from consent through construction.
•
Develop and implement consent management and compliance strategies to support project delivery and reduce environmental and regulatory risk.
•
Establish and maintain comprehensive consents, commitments, and obligations registers, ensuring requirements are clearly tracked and managed.
•
Provide oversight of consent compliance processes and ensure project teams understand and fulfil environmental commitments.
•
Coordinate the preparation and submission of applications for the discharge of requirements, planning conditions, and other consent-related obligations.

Act as the primary point of contact for consent and compliance queries from project teams, clients, contractors, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Liaise with regulatory bodies, including the Planning Inspectorate, Local Planning Authorities, Environment Agency, Natural England, and other statutory consultees.
•
Support and lead environmental compliance audits, inspections, and regulatory reviews.
•
Prepare clear and concise reports on compliance status, emerging risks, and consent-related matters for clients, regulators, and senior project leadership.
•
Collaborate closely with engineering, environmental, planning, legal, and construction teams to ensure effective integration of consent requirements into project delivery.
•
Support business development through proposal preparation, client engagement, presentations, and thought leadership initiatives.
•
Mentor and develop junior team members, contributing to a positive and collaborative team culture.
Why This Role Matters
The successful delivery of major infrastructure projects depends on effective environmental compliance and robust consent management. As a Principal Consultant, you will help clients navigate complex regulatory frameworks, maintain compliance throughout construction, and deliver projects responsibly and sustainably.
Your expertise will play a critical role in managing environmental risk, protecting project programmes, and ensuring projects achieve their objectives while meeting regulatory expectations and environmental commitments.
What We're Looking For
•
Experience in environmental consent management, post-consent compliance, or environmental project delivery within the UK infrastructure sector.
•
Degree (or equivalent qualification) in Environmental Management, Environmental Planning, Geography, Ecology, Engineering, Law, or a related discipline.
•
Proven experience supporting or leading the discharge of consent requirements, planning conditions, and environmental commitments on major infrastructure projects.
•
Strong understanding of UK planning and consenting regimes, including:
•
Development Consent Orders (DCOs)
•
Town and Country Planning Act
•
Electricity Act Section 36 Consents
•
Associated environmental permitting and licensing requirements
•
Knowledge of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), environmental legislation, and the practical implementation of mitigation and monitoring commitments during construction.
•
Excellent stakeholder management skills with experience engaging clients, regulators, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams.
•
Strong organisational and analytical skills, including management of complex compliance, legal, and regulatory requirements.
•
Experience preparing compliance reports, consent submissions, and regulatory correspondence.
•
Excellent communication, project management, and problem-solving skills.
Desirable
•
Experience managing environmental compliance during construction phases of major infrastructure projects.
•
Experience working within sectors such as transmission and distribution, renewable energy, hydrogen, solar, or wind.
•
Professional membership of a relevant institution (IEMA, RTPI, CIWEM, CEnv or equivalent).
•
Line management or mentoring experience.
What You'll Bring
You are a proactive and client-focused environmental professional with a strong understanding of post-consent project delivery. You combine technical knowledge with commercial awareness and are confident working with clients, regulators, and project teams to deliver successful outcomes. You thrive in a collaborative environment, enjoy solving complex challenges, and are passionate about helping infrastructure projects achieve high environmental standards.

On our programme you will engage with challenging and exciting project work, and deliver innovative business or technical solutions as part of a team of subject matter experts. Throughout the programme you will receive coaching and support from your team to achieve your objectives as well as your personal development goals. You will gain a wide array of experience on your placement that you can apply to your academic studies and future career.
At Leonardo we value individuals who continuously demonstrate a dedication to their personal development. We are looking for highly motivated individuals who are willing to take on a challenge to complete a placement, and we will demand a high degree of customer focus and work performance from you in order to meet our operational challenges. If you are willing to commit to giving your best performance, you will find Leonardo a very rewarding place to work!
Successful completion of an Industrial Placement with Leonardo may also lead to an offer on our Graduate Development Programme.
During your placement, we encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.
What you’ll do
Systems Engineers are involved in all aspects of design and development; from initial product design through to in-service support.
They look at the big picture, determine how the system needs to operate and collaborate to produce the required overall operational behaviours. They also dive into the deepest level of detail – taking the system piece-by-piece and defining its design to the finest point. Our Systems Engineers can also actively engage in R&D, developing new concepts and conducting fundamental research into our future technologies.
As a Industrial Placement Systems Engineer, you will work on real engineering problems within either the Radar or the Advanced Targeting business area. You will have the opportunity to be involved in supporting a wide range of tasks across multiple projects/products, such as:
• The radar for the Typhoon fighter jet
• The radar for the SAAB Gripen fighter
• Our family of Surveillance AESA (Active Electronically Scanned Array) radars
• An IRCM (Infra-Red Counter Measures) system
• Our laser target designator or laser ranging systems
Core activities within Systems Engineering include:
• Requirements capture, design documentation, verification and validation.
• Algorithm design and test.
• Performance modelling; building physics-based models to test our designs through computer simulation.
• Data analysis; end-to-end systems analysis using synthetic and ‘real world’ data.
• Applied research; from product improvements to blue-sky thinking.
You will work with an experienced engineer who will provide day-to-day guidance and on-the-job training. You will be introduced to systems engineering processes, methods, technology and tools, with particular emphasis placed on learning practical skills that may not be easily gained or experienced in the academic environment of a university.
What you’ll bring
All of our Industrial Placement roles require a minimum predicted 2:1 in relevant degree discipline such as Physics, Mathematics, Engineering, or other STEM subject degrees. This should be a minimum of a Bachelors level degree.
• Be a self-motivated individual, willing to take on new challenges and drive continuous personal development
• Strong communication skills across a variety of mediums i.e. written, verbal, digital, etc.
• The ability to develop effective working relationships with peers and stakeholders
• Adaptable to the ever-changing demands that will be encountered within the role
• Offer novel ideas and methods for solving technical problems, drawing on personal experiences and knowledge learned during academic studies
In addition to this, we would be interested in hearing from you if you have experience in:
• Coding/programming.
• Relevant project work and/or placements in industry.
• Solving problems as part of a team
• Applying your science and technology knowledge to solve a real-world problem
This is not an exhaustive list, and we are keen to hear from you even if you might not have experience in all of the above. The most important skill is a good attitude and willingness to learn.
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

Brown & Brown Claims
Brown & Brown is the 5th largest intermediary business in the world with over 23,000 teammates and offices throughout the US and Europe. Brown & Brown Claims is the in-house claims team responsible for handling claims on behalf of the international underwriting division. The department manages a diverse portfolio of household, commercial and liability claims, supporting customers from first notification of loss through to settlement while delivering excellent customer outcomes and maintaining strong insurer relationships.
Role Summary
Purpose of Role
Reporting directly to the Senior Claims Supervisor, the Liability Claims Handler is responsible for the investigation, validation, negotiation and settlement of Third-Party Property Damage (TPPD) claims arising under combined liability insurance policies.
Whilst the primary focus of the role is the handling of Third-Party Property Damage claims, the successful candidate will also manage a small allocation of lower-value Personal Injury claims. This will include minor injury and straightforward bodily injury matters, requiring the handler to assess medical evidence, evaluate quantum, consider causation and negotiate settlements in line with insurer philosophy and prevailing claims protocols. An understanding of personal injury claims handling principles is therefore highly desirable and will support effective management of the wider liability portfolio.
This is a technically focused claims handling role requiring a strong understanding of liability principles, insurance policy coverage, evidential requirements and litigation risk. The postholder will independently manage a caseload of claims ranging from straightforward incidents through to complex and disputed liability matters involving substantial third-party losses.
The Claims Handler will work closely with policyholders, claimants, brokers, insurers, solicitors, engineers, loss adjusters and other stakeholders to ensure claims are resolved efficiently whilst controlling indemnity spend, reducing lifecycle times and protecting insurer interests.

• Identify customer vulnerabilities and ensure all customers receive fair treatment in line with regulatory expectations.

Equities Technology at Citi is undertaking a bold, multi‑year transformation to build a best‑in‑class global platform across execution, prime, clearing and cross‑product margining. We are re‑engineering our technology estate to achieve world‑leading performance and resiliency, enabling new capabilities in advanced execution, global market connectivity, and modernised post‑trade, clearing and margin processes. Citi's Equities Technology organization is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join the Equities Electronic- Execution (Electronic Trading) technology team. The person in this role will be responsible for the design, development, and delivery of Citi's next-generation low-latency execution platform. • Agile & CI/CD: Contribute to and champion Agile development practices and Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) processes with a focus on shift-left testing and accelerated release cycles.
• Platform Support & Enhancement: Build and maintain common solutions for trading platform monitoring, trade reconciliation, application recovery, and other essential support functions.
What you will bring
• Extensive  experience with strong technical knowledge and expertise in Low Latency Java,
• Strong understanding of automated testing techniques and quality engineering practices.
• Solid understanding of Agile methodologies and Continuous Integration processes.
• Familiarity with low-latency system design, including performance optimization, concurrency, and high-throughput architecture.
• Ability to prioritize multiple tasks, set goals, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, globally distributed environment.
• Excellent communication skills with a demonstrable ability to present and grasp complex concepts in a multicultural, cross-regional environment.
• Knowledge of regional exchange microstructure and regulatory regimes.
Bonus points for:
• Coupled with extensive Java expertise, added programing skills and experience in C++ or Rust would be considered advantageous.
• Prior experience developing electronic trading platforms in a global financial institution or equivalent environment.

Are you passionate about making a difference and helping others?
Would you like to work in a role that puts the customer at the heart of everything we do, making a genuine positive impact?
Then consider the role of a Progression Coach at Reed in Partnership!
This role is office based, but will involve travel across the North East.
